607:
Smoking shall be prohibited in the following enclosed residential facilities:
(a) All private and semi-private rooms in nursing homes.
(b) All hotel and motel guest rooms.
(Ord. No. 2021-002, § 1, 1-12-2021)
608:
Smoking is prohibited within a reasonable distance of ten feet outside an enclosed area where smoking is prohibited, so as to ensure that tobacco smoke does not enter the area through entrances, windows, ventilation systems, or other means.
(Ord. No. 2021-002, § 1, 1-12-2021)
609:
Notwithstanding any other provision of this chapter to the contrary, the following areas shall be exempt from the provisions of sections 6-1005 through 6-1008:
(a) Private residences, except when used as a licensed childcare, adult day care, or health care facility.
(b) Outdoor areas except those covered by the provisions of section 6-1006.
(c) Restaurant patios.
(d) Cigar bars, which shall be defined for purposes of this section as an establishment licensed by the City to operate as a tobacco business, and/or with a pending application with the City for a license to operate as a tobacco business, as of November 1, 2020. A cigar bar meeting this exception must not allow patrons or employees who are under age 21 during any operational hours that smoking is permitted on the premises. This exemption shall be nontransferable and shall expire automatically should the establishment at any time cease operations for more than 30 days, change ownership or cease to allow smoking on the premises for a period of more than 30 days.
(e) Hookah bars, which shall be defined for purposes of this section as an establishment licensed by the City to operate as a tobacco business and/or drinking place legally as of November 1, 2020, that generated 20 percent or more of its total annual gross income from the on-site sale of hookah/shisha products for the calendar year ending December 31, 2020. A Hookah bar must not allow patrons or employees who are under age 21 during any operational hours that smoking is permitted on the premises. This exemption shall be nontransferable and shall expire automatically should the establishment cease operations for more than 30 days, change ownership or cease to allow smoking on the premises for a period of more than 30 days.
(Ord. No. 2021-002, § 1, 1-12-2021)
610:
Notwithstanding any other provision of this chapter, an owner, operator, manager, or other person in control of an establishment, facility, or outdoor area may declare that entire establishment, facility, or outdoor area as a nonsmoking place. Smoking shall be prohibited in any place in which a sign conforming to the requirements of subsection 6-10014(a) is posted.
(Ord. No. 2021-002, § 1, 1-12-2021)
611:
(a) "No smoking" signs or the international "no smoking" symbol consisting of a pictorial representation of a burning cigarette enclosed in a red circle with a red bar across it may be clearly and conspicuously posted by the owner, operator, manager, or other person in control in every public place and place of employment where smoking is prohibited by this chapter.
(b) All ashtrays and other smoking paraphernalia shall be removed from any area where smoking is prohibited by this chapter by the owner, operator, manager, or other person having control of the area. This does not prohibit these items for resale purposes.
(c) Unregulated establishments that allow smoking under section 6-10012, except for subsection (a), shall post conspicuously at every entrance a sign indicating that smoking is permitted.
(Ord. No. 2021-002, § 1, 1-12-2021)
612:
No person or employer shall discharge, refuse to hire, or in any manner retaliate against an employee, applicant for employment, or customer because that employee, applicant, or customer exercises any rights afforded by this chapter or reports or attempts to prosecute a violation of this chapter.
(Ord. No. 2021-002, § 1, 1-12-2021)
613:
(a) This chapter shall be enforced by an authorized designee of the city.
(b) Notice of the provisions of this chapter shall be given to all applicants for a business license in the city.
(c) Any citizen who desires to register a complaint under this chapter may initiate enforcement with police and code enforcement.
(d) Fire marshal or designee shall, while an establishment is undergoing otherwise mandated inspections, inspect for compliance with this chapter.
(e) An owner, manager, operator, or employee of an establishment regulated by this chapter shall inform persons violating this chapter of the appropriate provisions thereof.
(f) Notwithstanding any other provision of this chapter, an employee or private citizen may bring legal action to enforce this chapter.
(g) In addition to the remedies provided by the provisions of this section, the city manager or any person aggrieved by the failure of the owner, operator, manager, or other person in control of a public place or a place of employment to comply with the provisions of this chapter may apply for injunctive relief to enforce those provisions in any court of competent jurisdiction.
(Ord. No. 2021-002, § 1, 1-12-2021)
614:
(a) A person who smokes in an area where smoking is prohibited by this chapter shall be guilty of an infraction, punishable by a fine not exceeding $50.00.
(b) A person who owns, manages, operates, or otherwise controls a public place or place of employment and who fails to comply with the provisions of this chapter shall be guilty of an infraction, punishable by:
(1) A fine not exceeding $100.00 for a first violation.
(2) A fine not exceeding $200.00 for a second violation.
(3) A fine not exceeding $500.00 for each additional violation.
(c) In addition to the fines established by this section, violation of this chapter by a person who owns, manages, operates, or otherwise controls a public place or place of employment may result in the suspension or revocation of any permit or license issued to the person for the premises on which the violation occurred.
(d) Each day on which a violation of this chapter occurs shall be considered a separate and distinct violation.
(Ord. No. 2021-002, § 1, 1-12-2021)
615:
The city may engage in a continuing program to explain and clarify the purposes and requirements of this chapter to citizens affected by it, and to guide owners, operators, and managers in their compliance with it. The program may include publication of a brochure for affected businesses and individuals explaining the provisions of this chapter.
(Ord. No. 2021-002, § 1, 1-12-2021)
616:
The city manager shall annually request other governmental and educational agencies having facilities within the city to establish local operating procedures in cooperation and compliance with this chapter. This includes urging all federal, state, county, city, and school district agencies to update their existing smoking control regulations to be consistent with the current health findings regarding secondhand smoke.
(Ord. No. 2021-002, § 1, 1-12-2021)
617:
This chapter shall be liberally construed so as to further its purposes.
(Ord. No. 2021-002, § 1, 1-12-2021)
618:
Footnote 2:
Editor's note— Ord. No. 2023-014, § 1, adopted May 23, 2023, repealed the former Ch. 2, §§ 6-2001—6-2034, and enacted a new Ch. 2 as set out herein. The former Ch. 2 pertained to similar subject matter and derived from Ord. No. 2018-041, § 1, 10-23-2018.
619:
This chapter shall be known as the City of South Fulton Solid Waste Ordinance.
(Ord. No. 2023-014, § 1, 5-23-2023)
620:
The following words, terms, and phrases when used in this chapter shall have the following meanings ascribed to them, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:
In the event that there is a difference of interpretation of the provided definition and the intent as used or recognized in the solid waste trade and/or industry which cannot be reconciled or provide adequate clarification, thenthe legal opinion of the City Attorney may be sought to provide an opinion that shall be utilized.
Biomedical waste shall mean pathological waste, biological waste cultures and stocks of infectious agents and associated biologicals, contaminated animal carcasses (body parts, their bedding, and other wastes from such animals), sharps, chemotherapy waste, discarded medical equipment all parts, not including expendable supplies and materials which have not been decontaminated, as further defined in Georgia Department of Natural Resources, Environmental Protection Rule 391-3-4-.15, or as amended.
Bulk waste shall be defined as furniture, ranges, washers, sofas, car seats, play equipment, chairs, tables and other large "household" items which cannot reasonably be placed in a 95-gallon roll cart. Items not considered bulk waste include tires, batteries, yard debris, construction materials, propane tanks, windows & sliding glass doors, pool tables, safes, trampolines, mirrors and panes of glass, swing sets, pianos and any items too heavy or awkward that they cannot be safely lifted.
Collect or collection shall mean to remove residential solid waste, residential recovered materials, or commercial solid waste for transport to a disposal or processing facility, or cause such to be removed.
Collection services shall mean the collection from a residential unit or from a commercial establishment of municipal solid waste, and residential recovered materials including related transportation, transfer processing and/or disposal.
Commercial container shall mean a dumpster or similar waste receptacle supplied by a commercial service provider.
Commercial building shall mean a building or part of a building, which is used as shops, offices, business arcade, show rooms, display centers or market for sale of merchandise for retail only, building used for transaction of business or the keeping of accounts, records for similar purposes, professional service facilities, gas pumps, restaurants, cinemas, theaters, banks, or clubs run on commercial basis. Storage and service facilities incidental to the sale of merchandise shall be included under this group, except where exempted.
Commercial hand pick up shall mean any commercial development receiving residential service collections through the use of one or more roll carts.
Commercial property shall mean any hotel, motel, apartment dwelling consisting of more than four units, business, public or semi-public building or premises of any nature or kind whatsoever other than a residential service unit.
Commercial service provider shall mean a company authorized by the city to engage in commercial solid waste collection and disposal within the city.
Commercial solid waste shall mean all types of solid waste generated by stores, offices, restaurants, warehouses, and other nonmanufacturing activities, excluding residential, industrial, C&D, and hazardous wastes.
Commercial solid waste collection and disposal shall mean a company authorized under this chapter to collect, transport, and dispose and/or process commercial solid waste and commercial recovered materials in accordance with this chapter and other applicable laws related to commercial solid waste, commercial recovered materials, as well as incidental administrative tasks related to the performance of those requirements.
Composting shall mean the controlled biological decomposition of organic matter into stable, odor-free humus.
Construction and demolition waste (C&D waste) shall mean waste building materials and rubble resulting from construction, remodeling, repair, and demolition operations of pavements, houses, commercial buildings and other structures. Such waste includes, but is not limited, waste containing asbestos, wood, bricks, metal, concrete, wallboard, plywood, cardboard, carpeting, inert waste landfill material, and other non-putrescible waste, which have a low potential for groundwater contamination.
Cubic yard. Three feet high, by three feet deep, by three feet wide.
Customer means any firm, resident, owner, manager, entity, corporation or organization that contracts with a company for the collection and disposal of solid waste materials as defined in this chapter and including but not limited to construction/demolition debris, dead animals, solid waste, waste, storm debris, yard trimmings, and recyclable material.
Disabled person shall mean an owner of a residential service unit who is disabled to the extent that he or she is incapable of placing his or her residential municipal solid waste, storage cart, residential recovered materials, storage bin, bulk waste and/or yard trimmings at the residential designated collection location for collection by the residential service provider, such that he or she satisfies this chapter.
Disposal facility shall mean a sanitary landfill or other solid waste disposal facility permitted by the Georgia Department of Natural Resources, Environmental Protection Division and/or other applicable regulatory agency with jurisdiction and where the final deposition of solid waste occurs and includes but is not limited to landfilling and solid waste thermal treatment technology facilities.
Disposal shall mean dumping or depositing of solid waste into or onto a disposal facility.
Duplex shall mean a building designed exclusively for residential occupancy by two families.
Hazardous waste shall mean any solid waste which has been defined as a hazardous waste in regulations promulgated by the United States Environmental Protection Agency or under Georgia Hazardous Waste Management Act, O.C.G.A. § 12-8-60 et seq.
Household appliances such as refrigerators, stoves, washers, dryers, water heaters, and other large, enameled appliances, which do not contain polychlorinated biphenyls (PCB) or chlorofluorocarbon refrigerant (CFC) and have been officially certified to that effect, and in the case of refrigerators and freezers, which have had the doors removed.
Industrial materials/waste shall mean any solid waste or refuse; sludge from a wastewater treatment plant, water supply treatment plant, or air pollution control facility; and other discarded material including solid, liquid, semisolid, or contained gaseous material resulting from industrial, commercial, mining, and agricultural operations and from community activities, but does not include unacceptable waste; recovered materials; solid or dissolved materials in domestic sewage; solid or dissolved materials in irrigation return flows or industrial discharges that are point sources subject to permit under 33 U.S.C. Section 1342; or source, special nuclear, or by-product material as defined by the Federal Atomic Energy Act of 1954, as amended. Shall also mean solid waste generated by manufacturing or industrial processes or operations that is not a hazardous waste. Industrial waste also includes, but is not limited to, waste resulting from the following manufacturing processes. - electric power generations; food-related products and byproducts; inorganic chemicals; iron and steel products; leather and leather products; nonferrous metal and foundry products; organic chemicals, plastics and resins; pulp and paper; rubber and miscellaneous plastic products; stone, glass, clay, and concrete products; textiles; and other discarded parts and machinery.
Landfill shall mean an area of land on which or an excavation in which solid waste is placed for permanent disposal and which is not a land application unit, surface impoundment, injection well, or compost pile.
Multi-family dwelling shall mean a building designed exclusively for residential occupancy by more than one family, to include duplex, triplex, and quadraplex units or any connected dwelling.
Municipal solid waste shall mean any solid waste derived from households including solid waste, trash, and sanitary waste in septic tanks and means solid waste from, single-family and multifamily residences, hotels and motels, bunkhouses, campgrounds, picnic grounds, and day use recreation areas. The term includes yard trimmings and commercial solid waste but does not include construction and demolition waste and solid waste from mining, agricultural, or silvicultural operations or industrial processes or operations.
Municipal solid waste disposal facility shall mean any facility or location where the final deposition of any amount of municipal solid waste occurs, whether or not mixed with or including commercial or industrial solid waste, and includes, but is not limited to, municipal solid waste landfills and municipal solid waste thermal treatment technology facilities.
Non-curbside collection shall mean collection of residential municipal solid waste outside the residential designated collection location.
Owner shall mean any person, firm, corporation or other entity owning, leasing, renting, occupying, or managing any residential or commercial premises in the city.
Ownership shall mean ownership, leasing, renting, occupying, or managing any premises by any individual, firm, corporation or other entity in the city.
Plan shall mean the 2005 Comprehensive Solid Waste Management Plan developed for Fulton County for the area previously defined as the special services district for the areas that has is now incorporated as the City of South Fulton, as amended prior to the effective date of this ordinance. The plan is hereby adopted by the city through this ordinance and may be amended by resolution and/or ordinance by the city from time to time.
Plastic bag means any bag made with plastic, including biodegradable plastic or compostable plastic, but does not include a Reusable Bag;
Recovered materials shall mean those materials which have known use, reuse, or recycling potential; can be feasibly used, reused, or recycled; and have been diverted or removed from the solid waste stream for sale, use, reuse, or recycling whether or not requiring subsequent separation and processing.
Recovered materials processing facility (RMPF) shall mean a facility engaged solely in the storage, processing, and resale or reuse of recovered materials. Such term shall not include a solid waste handling facility; provided, however, any solid waste generated by such facility shall be subject to all applicable laws and regulations relating to such solid waste.
Recycling shall mean any process by which materials which would otherwise become solid waste are collected, separated, or processed and reused or returned to use in the form of raw materials or products, except for mixed municipal solid waste composting.
Residential designated collection location shall mean within six feet of the curb, paved surface of the public road, closest accessible public right-of-way, or other such location agreed to by the residential service provider for placement of the residential municipal solid waste storage cart, the residential recovered materials storage bin, and/or any yard trimmings, bulk waste, or white goods are placed, that will provide safe and efficient accessibility to the residential service provider's collection crew and vehicle.
Residential municipal solid waste shall mean municipal solid waste generated at a residential service unit.
Residential municipal solid waste storage cart shall mean a leak-proof container with attached lid and wheels that allow the automated or semi-automated collection of residential municipal solid waste that meets the specifications established by the city.
Residential recovered materials shall mean recovered materials generated at residential service units that have been diverted or removed from the residential municipal solid waste stream for sale, use, or recycling, whether or not requiring subsequent separation and processing.
Residential service provider shall mean a company authorized under this chapter to perform the physical process of collecting, transporting, and disposing of the residential municipal solid waste, residential recovered materials, and bulk waste and/or yard trimmings within the city.
Residential service unit shall mean each unit or units within the following categories that use single-family, residential-type waste storage containers and/or residential municipal solid waste storage carts. Single-family dwellings; duplexes; triplexes; quadraplexes; and mobile homes.
Residential solid waste shall mean food waste, including waste accumulations of animal or vegetable matter used or intended for use as food, or that attends the preparation, use, cooking, dealing in or storing of meat, fish, fowl, fruit or vegetables. Solid waste does not include unacceptable waste.
Roll cart shall mean a plastic, covered receptacle with an incorporated handle and wheels, used for receiving and holding solid waste, recyclables, or compostables with a normal capacity range between 20 and 95 gallons.
Selected residential service provider shall mean a company operating within the city pursuant to a contract under this chapter with the city.
Service provider shall mean the selected solid waste provider.
Single-family dwelling shall mean a detached building, or portion thereof, which is used exclusively for residential occupancy by one family.
Solid waste handling shall mean the storage, collection, transportation, treatment, utilization, processing, or disposal of solid waste or any combination of such activities.
Solid waste handling facility shall mean any facility the primary purpose of which is the storage, collection, transportation, treatment, utilization, processing, or disposal, or any combination thereof, of solid waste.
Special services shall, elective services, and city-sponsored events such as special neighborhood clean-up days that produce amounts of residential municipal solid waste, residential recovered materials, and yard trimmings.
Transfer station shall mean a facility, permitted by applicable law, used to transfer solid waste from one collection vehicle to another for transportation to a disposal facility or processing facility.
Unacceptable waste shall mean hazardous waste, biomedical waste, tires, paints, paint solvents, treated wood, un-emptied aerosol cans, compressed gas cylinders, large engine parts, small engines containing oils or fuels, chemicals, large glass panes, large tree debris, stumps, ammunition of any type, dead animals larger than ten pounds, firearms, and any and all waste of which the acceptance and handling by a residential service provider or commercial service provider would cause a violation of any permit condition, legal or regulatory requirement, substantial damage to the service providers equipment or facilities, or present a substantial danger to the health or safety of the public or the service provider's employees.
Yard debris shall mean leaves, brush, grass clippings, shrub and tree pruning, discarded Christmas trees, nursery and greenhouse vegetative residuals, and vegetative matter resulting from landscaping development and maintenance other than mining, agricultural, and silvicultural operations.
(Ord. No. 2023-014, § 1, 5-23-2023; Ord. No. 2023-034, § 1, 10-10-2023)
622:
(a) The city shall be exclusively responsible for the collection and disposal of all solid waste, and bulk waste within the city limits.
(b) Solid waste collection service shall be provided for by the city either on its own or through independent service providers operating except as follows:
(1) The city shall not be responsible for the collection, hauling and disposing of any type of solid waste originating from professional debris removal services or items generated outside the city, or property regulated by federal, state, or county governments.
(2) There may be joint or multiple use of solid waste containers by outside collection services, subject to securing a permit or contract therefore from the city council and pursuant to rules and regulations therefore as established by the city council.
(Ord. No. 2023-014, § 1, 5-23-2023)
623:
(a) It shall be mandatory for all occupants or persons in possession, charge or control of homes, buildings and premises in the city or from which solid waste is created, accumulated or produced to use the collection service provided by the city.
(b) Every residence within the city will be provided solid waste collections and disposal services from the city at a fee established by the city council.
(c) Exception. The city manager, or designee, shall be authorized to allow additional service providers to negotiate directly with properties classified as industrial with special service requirements or own by a federal, state, or county government.
(Ord. No. 2023-014, § 1, 5-23-2023)
624:
(a) All solid waste shall be placed in bags securely closed and stored in solid waste authorized containers.
(b) The total content within the bags shall not exceed the strength of the bag. The total weight placed in a container shall not exceed the weight noted on the container. If no limit is noted, the weight shall be set at 65 lbs.
(c) Any solid waste that may injure or hamper a collector, such as, but not limited to, potentially sharp or dangerous objects shall be securely wrapped to prevent puncture of the bag/wrapping or solid waste container.
(d) If an authorized solid waste container is obstructed in such a manner so as to prohibit the collection vehicle from dumping the container, the container's contents will not be collected and/or an additional charge may be imposed for any additional effort to collect such waste.
(e) Waste placed in containers other than authorized containers will not be collected and the property owner will be subject to penalties if the containers are not removed within the specified timeframe.
(f) Liquids shall be limited to small amounts trapped within containers.
(Ord. No. 2023-014, § 1, 5-23-2023)
625:
(a) Collection of solid waste shall be made at least once a week from private residences, and as many times per week as the city businesses may order in accordance with specified contracts with city approved service providers.
(b) No Service Provider shall make residential collections between the hours of 7:00 p.m. and 6:00 a.m.
(c) The city manager, or designee, may adjust the times of service to accommodate special events or during declared emergencies.
(Ord. No. 2023-014, § 1, 5-23-2023)
626:
(a) No refuse or waste shall be stored on public property at any time, except within 24 hours prior to collection as provided in this chapter, and no refuse or waste shall be stored upon any private property other than that owned or occupied by the property in an approved method.
(b) Unauthorized accumulation. Any accumulation of refuse/waste on any premises in violation of this chapter is declared to be a nuisance and is prohibited and subject to penalties.
(Ord. No. 2023-014, § 1, 5-23-2023)
627:
(a) No person, company, service provider, corporation, property owner, or other entity shall violate the requirements set forth in this chapter.
(b) No person or entity shall collect solid waste in a manner which will be conducive to insect and rodent infestation or the harboring and feeding of animals; impair the air quality; impair the quality of the ground or surface waters; impair the quality of the environment; or likely create other hazards to the public health, safety, or well-being as defined by Georgia Department of Natural Resources, Environmental Protection Rule 391-3-4-04 or other applicable environmental codes.
(c) No person other than the occupant or owner thereof shall utilize any container placed for the purpose of storing solid waste pending collection, or remove or take any of the contents thereof, or remove any container from the location where the container has been placed by the owner thereof.
(d) No person shall discard or deposit any solid waste on the land of another without first obtaining permission of the owner in accordance with legislation established to regulate solid waste.
(e) No person shall discard or deposit, or permit the discarding or depositing, of any solid waste on any public right-of-way, except in receptacles provided for the purpose of holding such solid waste or exceptions as noted by this chapter.
(f) No person shall deposit any burning or smoldering material in waste or litter containers, or receptacles located in the city limits.
(g) No person shall set fire to the contents of any container, scatter the contents thereof or otherwise vandalize, damage or destroy such container or receptacle.
(h) No person shall deposit large items in containers exceeding the specified weight or preventing the lid to be securely closed.
(i) No solid waste may be disposed of by any person in an open dump, nor may any person cause, suffer, allow or condone open dumping or the burying of waste on their property as defined by Georgia Department of Natural Resources, Environmental Protection Rule 391-3-4-04 without a permit authorized by the City of South Fulton or other government with jurisdictional authority.
(j) No dead animal greater than one pound shall be deposited in any city authorized container. All dead animals shall be disposed in a method applicable by State laws.
(Ord. No. 2023-014, § 1, 5-23-2023)
628:
The removal of clothing, bedding or other refuse from places where infectious diseases or biomedical waste have prevailed shall be decontaminated prior to removal under the supervision and direction of the Fulton County Health Department or appropriate agency. Such refuse shall not be placed in containers for city collection until decontaminated.
(Ord. No. 2023-014, § 1, 5-23-2023)
629:
(a) No owner or occupant shall allow the accumulation on premises under their control or on or about any commercial establishment any solid waste where such solid waste creates a health hazard to neighbors or other citizens or is unsightly or emits foul or obnoxious odors which constitute either a public or private nuisance. Such conduct shall constitute a violation of this Ordinance.
(b) No person or entity shall place into a residential container any tires, paint cans, vehicle batteries, mercury-containing items, asbestos, or like items.
(c) It shall be a violation of this chapter to place or cause to be placed for collection by a residential service provider or commercial service provider any acid, explosive material, flammable liquids or dangerous or corrosive material of any kind.
(Ord. No. 2023-014, § 1, 5-23-2023)
630:
All construction and demolition contractors shall provide on-site refuse receptacles, bulk containers, or detachable containers for loose debris, paper, building material waste, scrap building materials, and other trash produced by those working at the construction site. The site shall be kept in a litter-free condition. The number of bulk containers or dumpsters shall be determined by the size and/or type of the job.
(Ord. No. 2023-014, § 1, 5-23-2023)
631:
(a) The city shall not be responsible for the collecting or hauling of building material originating from private property preliminary to, during or subsequent to the construction of new building, alterations or additions to an existing building of whatever type or from demolition of existing structures. Such material shall be removed by the owner of the property at their expense.
(b) Such materials shall not be placed on public property unless designated in accordance with an applicable building permit issued by the City of South Fulton.
(Ord. No. 2023-014, § 1, 5-23-2023)
632:
It shall be unlawful for any person to deposit any solid waste, trash, dirt or dead animals in any container provided or maintained by any owner, occupant or tenant or lessee using or occupying any building or commercial businesses, in any quantity to avoid providing or subscribing to a service for the pickup of such solid waste at the residence or the site of the operations of the business of such persons.
(Ord. No. 2023-014, § 1, 5-23-2023)
633:
The city recognizes that the service providers will not provide services on the designated dates and/or holidays which will be observe which are up to six holidays to include: New Year's Day, Thanksgiving Day, Christmas Day, and three other holidays as specified by the city manager. When a holiday is scheduled, customers will be provided an alternative collection date.
(Ord. No. 2023-014, § 1, 5-23-2023)
634:
(a) A written verification by a medical doctor that the resident is unable to physically place containers at the curbside may qualify the residential property to receive non-curbside container assistance. Residents requesting assistance must live alone or all persons living in household must be unable to assist with placing the containers curbside.
(b) Residences receiving assistance with the non-curbside service will utilize a collection point designated by the city's service provider which shall be located on the outside of the residence. The Service Provider shall not enter inside a private residence or open a secured location in order to remove solid waste.
(c) Any materials in the provided container shall be in a closed plastic bag. Each bag must not exceed 30 pounds and must fit within thecontainer. Extra bags lying around the roll cart may not be collected.
(d) Containers must be visible from the roadway and may be limited to a distance from the public roadway if specialized equipment has limited access.
(e) A disability form may be required by the city and will be available by contacting the City of South Fulton Solid Waste Coordinator.
(f) The age of the resident shall not be the sole determining factor but may be considered for those over the age of 65 and living alone.
(g) Collection assistance is not available for non-residential units or multifamily units utilizing a dumpster.
(Ord. No. 2023-014, § 1, 5-23-2023)
636:
(a) Each residential property shall be provided a 95-gallon roll cart container for household solid waste disposal. Additional roll carts may be leased by agreement with the residential service provider.
(b) If approved by city council and economically feasible for the city, each residential property shall be provided a roll cart for recycling. The recycling container will be marked differently from the solid waste container. See also section 6-2008 - Recycling and green initiatives.
(1) Only recyclable items identified by the city or service provider shall be placed in the recycling container.
(2) Due to market conditions the city council may limit or suspend recycling services as a provided city service.
(c) All owners/lessees of residential units shall keep the containers in a clean, neat and sanitary condition at all times.
(Ord. No. 2023-014, § 1, 5-23-2023)
637:
(a) Authorized containers assigned to residential or commercial customers are and shall remain property of the service provider.
(b) Damage due to, loss, or removal of an authorized container assigned to a residential or commercial unit shall be the responsibility of the property owner at the time such damage, loss or removal is discovered by the city or service provider.
(c) Persons moving shall leave all authorized containers at the location to which the containers have been assigned.
(d) In the event that the container is damaged due to the city or service provider's negligence or determined to be a defective container, a replacement container shall be provided to the owner of the property at no charge within ten (10) business days of being reported.
(e) All containers deemed to have been damaged by someone other than the city or service provider shall be billed to the property owner in-full. Payment shall be received in full prior to delivery.
(f) Loss containers shall be billed at the actual cost to replace the container.
(Ord. No. 2023-014, § 1, 5-23-2023)
638:
(a) Each container shall be maintained in as sanitary condition as is reasonably possible and shall not be allowed to create strong, offensive or noxious odors, serve as an insect or rodent feeding area or habitat, become unsightly or cause other conditions which would constitute a nuisance.
(b) Containers shall not be altered, painted, or modified.
(c) No holes shall be drilled into the container to allow fluids to escape.
(d) Containers shall only be used for the intended purpose.
(Ord. No. 2023-014, § 1, 5-23-2023)
639:
(a) Not all replacement containers shall be considered new but will be delivered clean and in working condition.
(b) The city or service provider is not obligated to provide a new container due to the current container being dirty or not maintained by the current or previous owner.
(c) A property owner being billed for solid waste may request a new container to replace the current container at a cost of 50 percent of the actual cost of the new container. The city or service provider will honor this request twice per calendar year per paid property.
(Ord. No. 2023-014, § 1, 5-23-2023)
640:
(a) The city or service provider is authorized to inspect all provided containers located on public property between the hours of 7:00 am and 7:00 pm Monday through Friday.
(b) The city or service provider shall be authorized to remove any container found to be in violation of this chapter.
(c) The property owner will receive notification within five business days of any removed containers and the reasons why the container was removed.
(Ord. No. 2023-014, § 1, 5-23-2023)
641:
The lids or covers of all solid waste containers shall always be kept secure and fastened so that flies and other insects may not have access to the contents thereof. While placed for collections, the lids should be securely closed and no contents within the containers should be visible.
(Ord. No. 2023-014, § 1, 5-23-2023)
642:
(a) Residential premises. With respect to residential premises, no solid waste containers or other containers other than those of the city or service provider, shall be placed or located within the right-of-way of a street or alley or at a distance exceeding two feet from the edge of street right-of-way.
(b) No container shall be placed within three feet of a mailbox, fire hydrant, or block any access to a sidewalk or driveway, where additional spacing is available.
(c) Containers shall only be placed along public roads during authorized times. All containers shall be placed no earlier than 24 hours prior to the scheduled pick up and shall be removed no longer than 24 hours following collection of all waste and recycling containers. The same standard shall be used for all bulky trash. Allowable yard debris shall be placed no earlier than 72 hours prior to collection of the same.
(d) Private streets and other roads which are not dedicated streets, roadways or city rights-of-way shall be fully accessible to the city or service provider and equipment in order for collections to be made in an unobstructed fashion. The city reserves the right to select an alternative location for collection when private roads are not suitable.
(e) Only authorized containers shall be placed within the city for collections.
(f) Commercial and industrial premises. With respect to commercial and industrial premises, containers shall be kept on the premises at a place approved by the city, readily accessible to collection vehicles.
(Ord. No. 2023-014, § 1, 5-23-2023)
643:
(a) Dumpsters, and compactors shall be the responsibility of and maintained by the owner of such property in a clean, disinfected, and sanitary manner so as to prevent the breeding of insects, vermin, or vectors, and/or the release of odors.
(b) All new dumpsters installed for residential and commercial properties after the effective date of this chapter shall be screened from view by a decorative masonry wall one foot taller than the dumpster on three sides and provide an operable gate for collection. In-ground compactors shall be screened by landscaping. Above ground compactors shall be screened by decorative masonry wall one foot taller than the compactor on three sides and provide an operable gate for collection. Temporary dumpsters provided for construction or special events (less than 30 days), are excluded from this requirement. This section does not substitute or remove any additional conditions required under applicable building or zoning codes.
(Ord. No. 2023-014, § 1, 5-23-2023)
644:
(a) It shall be unlawful for any person to throw, deposit or otherwise leave trash in dumpsters that are leased and paid for, for private use, except by permission of the owner. This prohibition includes dumpsters on city property. Only dumpsters marked "For Public Use" shall be used as intended. Solid waste and items placed outside a dumpster shall constitute litter.
(b) It shall be unlawful for any person to scavenge or remove solid waste from dumpsters. Solid waste and materials placed within dumpsters are the property of the company providing the service and the owner on file.
(Ord. No. 2023-014, § 1, 5-23-2023)
647:
(a) Adoption by reference. O.C.G.A. § 16-7-43 "Dumping, depositing, etc. litter on public or private property or waters" is hereby adopted with like effect as if recited herein.
(b) Enforcement. Unless expressly prohibited by other law, the enforcement provisions contained in O.C.G.A. § 16-7-45 is hereby adopted with like effect as if recited herein.
(Ord. No. 2023-014, § 1, 5-23-2023)
648:
(a) It shall be unlawful for any person to throw or deposit or cause to be thrown or deposited upon the streets, sidewalks, lanes or alleys or to any storm sewer, catch basin or drainage ditch, any paper, plastic, food waste, tree limbs, grass cuttings, yard debris, bulk waste, or other garbage/waste materials.
(b) No person shall deposit on or bury in, or cause to be deposited on or buried in, any of the land, public square, street, alley, lanes, vacant or unoccupied lot, or into any lake or watercourse, any noxious filth, odors or offensive liquid, solid material within the limits of the city except in standard approved garbage receptacles from which regular collections are made.
(Ord. No. 2023-014, § 1, 5-23-2023)
649:
An adequate number of vehicles shall be provided by the commercial and residential contractors to service its city customers. All such vehicles shall be licensed in the state and shall operate in compliance with all applicable state, federal and municipal regulations. All vehicles and other equipment shall be kept in proper repair and sanitary condition. Each vehicle shall have at least one broom and shovel to clean up solid waste that may be spilled or otherwise scattered during the process of collection. All vehicles shall be sufficiently secure so as to prevent any littering of solid waste and/or leakage of fluid. No vehicle shall be willfully overloaded. Each vehicle shall be operated by a qualified driver holding a valid license of the category required to operate such vehicles.
(Ord. No. 2023-014, § 1, 5-23-2023)
650:
(a) It is unlawful to place any litter or other debris within the city's streams, bodies of water, or stormwater systems.
(b) It shall be unlawful for any person to dump, deposit, throw or leave or to cause or permit the dumping, depositing, placing, throwing or leaving of litter on any public or private property within the city unless:
(1) The property is designated by the state or by any of its agencies or political subdivisions for the disposal of such solid waste, and such person is authorized by the proper public authority to use such property.
(2) The litter is placed into a receptacle or container installed on such property; or
(3) The person is the owner or tenant in lawful possession of such property or has first obtained consent of the owner or tenant in lawful possession, or unless the act is done under the personal direction of the owner or tenant, all in a manner consistent with the public welfare.
(Ord. No. 2023-014, § 1, 5-23-2023)
651:
(a) No person shall operate any motor vehicle with items on or in such vehicle unless the items on or in such vehicle is adequately secured to prevent the dropping or shifting of materials from such load onto the roadway.
(b) It is the responsibility of the vehicle owner to secure all loose items such as paper, cardboard, plastic or similar items from leaving the vehicle.
(c) It shall be unlawful to drive or operate a vehicle in the city hauling wet litter or waste which vehicle allows such material to leak, flow freely or spill from such vehicle.
(d) Any litter or waste hauled on a moving vehicle in the city shall be placed in an enclosed area of the vehicle or covered or secured by a tarpaulin or other form of covering or restraint device adequately tied or anchored in such a manner that the litter or waste will not blow or escape from such vehicle while such vehicle is moving or is parked on public or private streets or roadways in the city.
(e) Vehicles used for the collection and transportation of waste or litter in the city shall be maintained in good repair, have watertight, metal bodies of easily cleanable construction, and shall be kept sufficiently clean so as to prevent the creation of offensive or noxious odors, insect or rodent habitation, unsightly conditions or other conditions that would constitute a nuisance.
(f) The operator of the offending vehicle shall be cited for any violation of this section.
(Ord. No. 2023-014, § 1, 5-23-2023)
652:
Whenever litter is thrown, deposited, dropped or dumped from any vehicle, boat, or other conveyance in violation of this chapter, it shall be prima facie evidence that the operator of the conveyance has violated this section of the city ordinance.
(Ord. No. 2023-014, § 1, 5-23-2023)
653:
The public works director, or designee shall establish and maintain receptacles for the deposit of litter at appropriate locations within the city where the property is frequented by the public. No receptacle will be placed on private property by the city.
(Ord. No. 2023-014, § 1, 5-23-2023)
654:
(a) All businesses open to the public shall place and maintain a container to deposit trash on the outside of the business. Businesses sharing a single property location will be counted as a single business for the purpose of this section.
(b) The owner or occupant of any business or commercial property within the city shall at all times keep their premises clean of trash, paper, cartons, package containers and other used or waste materials thrown or left on such premises and to prevent the same drifting or blowing to adjoining premises.
(Ord. No. 2023-014, § 1, 5-23-2023)
656:
(a) Residential customers may contract for yard waste collections through the city's designated provider or from a licensed collector.
(b) Property owners are responsible for the removal of lose debris left behind after collections within three days. Items placed or washed into a stormwater drain will be considered a violation.
(Ord. No. 2023-014, § 1, 5-23-2023)
657:
All residents utilizing collections of yard debris shall place such items on their premises behind the curb line, located so as to be easily accessible to street pickup and shall be placed at least three feet from fixed items such as fire hydrants, telephone poles or electrical boxes, water meters, mailboxes or anything that could be damaged by equipment or personnel picking up said items.
(Ord. No. 2023-014, § 1, 5-23-2023)
658:
All holders of a tree service license or any person engaging in the cutting of trees/vegetation for hire or compensation shall be required to remove all debris, brush and limbs. It shall be unlawful for any person to trim or remove trees within the city unless the byproduct from those services is immediately removed from the premises and properly disposed of.
This section shall apply to all debris which exceeds the definition of yard debris acceptable for monthly collection by the city noted in section 6-2007.2.
(Ord. No. 2023-014, § 1, 5-23-2023)
659:
(a) Bulk waste from residences may be placed at curbside for collection during a designated service once per month. One cubic yard will be collected per designed visit monthly for each active residential account at no additional charge.
(b) All residents utilizing city collection of bulk waste shall place such items on their premises behind the curb line, located so as to be easily accessible to street pickup, not to be placed over or next to fixed items such as fire hydrants, telephone poles or electrical boxes, water meters, mailboxes or anything that could be damaged by equipment or personnel picking up said items. The city and its collection service provider will not be responsible for repairing or replacing items removed or damaged which were placed curbside in such a manner that it appeared to be intended for removal or was not visible because it was mixed with other items placed curbside.
(c) Bulk waste placed curbside outside of the designated week of the month and/or exceeding the one cubic yard per month shall be picked up at a cost of $75.00 per cubic yard and billed to the property owner.
(Ord. No. 2023-014, § 1, 5-23-2023)
660:
Composting is allowed and permitted pursuant to this article for residential property that consists of a minimum of 22,000 square feet and can be placed at a minimum of 15 feet from a real property line in the rear of the property. Composting shall be maintained in accordance with city ordinances to avoid any nuisances.
(Ord. No. 2023-014, § 1, 5-23-2023)
661:
(a) The city will remove one natural holiday tree up to 15 feet in length per residential unit during the first two full weeks in January. These items can be set out for collection on the resident's regular collection day.
(b) Holiday trees shall be placed off the road in a manner that does not block road, sidewalks, or stormwater drains/ditches.
(c) Residents shall remove decorations such as wires, lights, stands, and tinsel from the tree.
(Ord. No. 2023-014, § 1, 5-23-2023)
662:
(a) Bulk waste disposal shall not apply to multi-family or commercial properties. Removal of bulk waste shall be the responsibility of the property owner when excluded from city collections.
(b) The city council or by and through the city manager, reserves the right to suspend collections based on pending weather conditions, service agreement, or fiscal constraints.
(Ord. No. 2023-014, § 1, 5-23-2023)
664:
The city council finds that it is in the best interest of the citizens of the city, in order to promote the health, safety and welfare of the citizens to recycle as many waste materials as possible in order to reduce the accumulation of litter and waste within the city and to reduce the overall solid waste materials which must be properly disposed of; therefore, it is the policy of the city to encourage recycling whenever practicable.
(Ord. No. 2023-014, § 1, 5-23-2023)
665:
The city may from time to time provide, or cause to be provided through their service provider, collection bins for collection of recyclable material. Upon receipt of a collection bin, each owner/lessee shall keep such collection bin in a clean, neat and sanitary condition at all times. In the event any collection bin becomes lost, destroyed or damaged, or otherwise unusable for the collection of recyclable materials, said owner/lessee shall reimburse the city for the cost for replacing such collection bin.
(Ord. No. 2023-014, § 1, 5-23-2023)
666:
The city encourages service providers to utilize green energy vehicles such as natural gas, electric, and hydrogen fuel sources. During the selection of a service provider the city council reserves the right to add a preference towards providers that have the ability to utilize green energy vehicles and/or facilities. Other preferences may be awarded for utilizing recyclable materials in provided residential carts.
(Ord. No. 2023-014, § 1, 5-23-2023)
668:
No individual, partnership, corporation or other entity shall collect and dispose of municipal solid waste without obtaining a tax occupation certificate to provide service from the city.
(Ord. No. 2023-014, § 1, 5-23-2023)
669:
(a) Service providers are instructed to remove only the contents located within the authorized containers and yard trimmings and bulk waste placed at the curb in accordance with section 6-2007.
(b) In accordance with section 6-2012, the city or its service provider shall be notified by the customer a minimum of two business days before the day of collection if additional services are requested. The city or its contractor will determine the charge according to the amount of material to be removed.
(Ord. No. 2023-014, § 1, 5-23-2023)
670:
(a) A performance bond shall be posted with the city by the registered or contracted solid waste hauler for the purpose of covering the cost of continued collection and disposal of waste and recyclable materials for the hauler's customers in the event a registered hauler abandons service.
(b) Each waste hauler shall present said performance bond equal to an amount to cover a minimum of 60 days of waste collection and disposal at the time of an approved and executed agreement. Said amount shall be maintained for the term of the executed agreement.
(Ord. No. 2023-014, § 1, 5-23-2023)
671:
(a) The service provider shall not transfer, assign, sell or convey any rights granted under any resulting agreement from this chapter without the prior written approval of the city council.
(b) The service provider may, upon 90 day written notice to the city manager, transfer the agreement to a wholly owned subsidiary of the service provider; provided the terms of the executed agreement is not altered and the city council has voted to approve the transfer.
(c) This section shall not apply to vehicles, replacements, maintenance, upgrades or modifications of equipment, machinery, containers and buildings by service provider for the purpose of maintaining and continuing its operation within the city.
(Ord. No. 2023-014, § 1, 5-23-2023)
672:
(a) At the time of submission of a signed authorized service agreement and prior to engaging in solid waste handling in the city and annually thereafter, each service provider shall provide as a requirement of the awarded contract proof of minimum insurance as follows:
(1) Comprehensive general liability insurance in the amount of $1,000,000.00.
(2) Vehicle liability as follows:
a. A limit of $500,000.00 per occurrence for bodily injury and property damage.
b. Comprehensive covering all owned, non-owned, and hired vehicles.
c. All insurance contracts must specify vehicles for solid waste collection.
(3) Umbrella liability insurance coverage at least as broad primary coverage in an amount of $1,000,000.00.
(b) All comprehensive general liability, vehicle liability, and umbrella liability policies shall show the city as an additional insured and shall provide for 60 days' notice of cancellation to the city manager.
(c) The mayor and city council with advice from the city attorney may increase the listed minimum requirements at the time of selection.
(Ord. No. 2023-014, § 1, 5-23-2023)
673:
(a) It is the service provider's obligation and responsibility to educate all customers on industry trends and best practices relating to solid waste collection, removal, and disposal. Such education programs must consist of the following elements: recycling; holiday schedules; new customer information; and any service-related items.
(b) All service providers have the obligation to inform customers of any non-collected trash or items placed for collection by the customer. Further, it is the service provider's obligation and responsibility to educate customers on days of collection for each specific service provided.
(c) All mass notifications directed to customers shall be sent through official communications to the city manager or designee at a minimum of three business days prior to sending to city residents and/or businesses.
(Ord. No. 2023-014, § 1, 5-23-2023)
675:
(a) All businesses and industries located in the city shall place all the solid waste generated by them in containers. All commercial containers must have close-fitting lids. All lids and side doors shall be kept closed by the users, so the contents are covered at all times.
(b) All containers shall be stored on private property and may not interfere with vehicular or pedestrian traffic. In the event that a container is placed on city property a lease agreement shall be first entered into with the city.
(Ord. No. 2023-014, § 1, 5-23-2023)
676:
(a) In order for the city to provide adequate service to the city for the collection, removal and disposal of accumulated refuse, the city may enter into a contract with an independent contractor, either private or another municipal corporate entity, for such services. In such event, any contract entered into shall be required to meet the standards and regulations of this chapter; provided, however, that the service provider shall have the right to offer specific services to all commercial or industrial customers which may involve specialized trucks, compactors, machinery or handling. Under such circumstances, all commercial or industrial customers using such services commonly referred to as roll-off services shall be subject to rates negotiated between the contractor and the building owners and/or occupants and shall be billed directly by the contractor.
(b) For items requiring special handling due to size, weight, type of material, or method of placement, the charges are to be negotiated between the contractor and the generator/owner prior to collection, and such service fees shall be billed directly to the customer from the contractor.
(c) In the event the city enters into a contract with a service provider for the collection of refuse throughout the city, such contract, once approved, shall be adopted by resolution and published in the office of the city clerk.
(Ord. No. 2023-014, § 1, 5-23-2023)
677:
(a) It shall be unlawful for any commercial/industrial solid waste contractor (hereinafter "commercial contractor") to provide commercial solid waste collection and disposal services within the city without first obtaining a city solid waste collection permit. Contractors desiring to perform such services shall make written application to the city for a permit on forms prescribed by the public works director.
(b) All applications shall be accompanied by a $500.00 application fee to defray investigative, administrative and regulatory costs. Permits shall be issued to qualified applicants for a twenty-four-month period from the time the application is approved. Each commercial contractor issued a permit shall pay a quarterly franchise fee as provided in section 6-2010.4.
(c) Commercial contractors desiring to renew their permits shall file renewal applications accompanied by a $500.00 renewal application fee. The renewal application shall be submitted on forms prescribed by the public works director on or before 60 days before expiration.
(d) The permit holder shall not transfer, assign, sell or convey any rights granted under any resulting agreement from this chapter without the prior written approval of the city council.
(Ord. No. 2023-014, § 1, 5-23-2023)
678:
(a) Each commercial contractor shall pay a franchise fee to be set by the city council from time to time per cubic yard of solid waste removed from the city, payable quarterly in accordance with reporting procedures adopted.
(b) The commercial franchise fee shall be established at ten percent unless specifically noted and executed in an agreement. A reduction less than ten percent shall be agreed to annual by a vote of the entire council annually.
(c) Every permitted commercial contractor is required to provide dependable solid waste service to customers within the city. Failure to provide dependable service may result in fines and/or permit revocation.
(d) Permit decal, name, address and phone number of the firm required on containers. Each commercial refuse container, recycling container, stationary compactor, and industrial waste container serviced by a commercial solid waste or recycling firm shall have affixed in a conspicuous place a distinctive red decal issued by the City of South Fulton which shows it is authorized to operate in the city. Commercial solid waste or recycling firms authorized to provide service within the city shall obtain decals from city and shall place them on the containers that they service. In addition, each commercial refuse container, recyclables container, stationary compactor, or waste container shall carry in a conspicuous place the name, telephone number and address of the firm authorized to service it. Distinctive decals shall be placed on commercial refuse containers.
(Ord. No. 2023-014, § 1, 5-23-2023)
679:
Not less than 30 days prior to commencing service, each commercial contractor shall furnish for the city's approval the initial schedules and maps of all routes to be used in servicing the commercial contractor's city customers. Any charges in routes and/or schedules shall also be subject to the director's approval, which will not be unreasonably withheld. The commercial contractor shall only undertake collections during the city's normal hours of collection, as adopted from time to time by the director. Exceptions may be made only upon the mutual agreement of the director and the commercial contractor. The commercial contractor shall also comply with all applicable city ordinances, including the city's noise ordinances.
(Ord. No. 2023-014, § 1, 5-23-2023)
681:
(a) Within 30 days following the close of each calendar quarter ending March 31, June 30, September 30, and December 31 of each year of operation, the solid waste service provider shall submit to the city manager reports of operation showing the following:
(1) Gross collection revenues and average number of customers during the quarter by service type.
(2) Tonnage figures showing the total waste tonnage collected by service type.
(3) Tonnage figures showing total recovered materials collected by type and proof of recycling in the form of manifests, bills of sale or other records showing adequate proof of movement of the material to a recycling facility as provided in this article.
(4) Proof of disposal of unrecovered materials at state-approved disposal facilities and the name of each such facility.
(b) The service provider shall maintain at its place of business books and records showing the names and addresses of all owners and tenants with whom the service provider contracted for solid waste handling services, including the street address for the property served. The service provider shall submit upon reasonable request of the city manager to a financial audit by a certified public accountant or auditor employed by the city.
(Ord. No. 2023-014, § 1, 5-23-2023)
683:
(a) The owner or occupant of any premises, office, business establishment, institution or industry or similar commercial establishment, shall be responsible for the collection and transportation of all solid waste accumulated at such premises, establishment or facility to a solid waste handling facility operating in compliance with state regulation and must arrange for service with an approved service provider.
(b) No business license or renewal thereof shall be issued until the owner or occupant of such premises provides the city business license office with the name of the service provider which provides collection for the business, or an exception has been granted by the city manager.
(c) The city reserves the right at all times to direct and control the time, place and manner of commercial solid waste handling. Nothing in this article is intended to abridge the city's right to ownership and control of the waste stream.
(d) Each service provider shall be responsible for all billing and invoicing to and collecting of service fees from its customers.
(e) The city shall maintain all approved commercial providers in the office of the city clerk and shall make available to businesses annually with business licenses renewals.
(Ord. No. 2023-014, § 1, 5-23-2023)
684:
(a) Authorization to provide solid waste services may be terminated by mutual agreement of the city and service provider at any time. Service providers may terminate authorization and surrender their permit to provide services by giving 60 days' notice to the city manager and furnishing proof to the city manager that all advance payments have been used by providing a service or have been refunded.
(b) The city manager shall notify any service provider of its violations of this article. Upon notification of the alleged violation, a service provider shall have ten calendar days to comply with any directive of the city manager to correct any such violation.
(c) At the discretion of the city manager, a hearing shall be held before the mayor and city council with the service provider being notified in writing of the time and place of the hearing and the violations of this article which have not been corrected. The service provider will be given the opportunity to appear by representative or counsel to answer any such charge. Should the mayor and city council determine by a majority vote that any of the sections of this chapter have been violated by the service provider, the mayor and city council shall have, in its discretion, the absolute right to suspend or revoke the authorization to provide service or provide for probation for the service provider.
(d) Authorization to provide services is nontransferable.
(Ord. No. 2023-014, § 1, 5-23-2023)
686:
In order for the city to provide adequate service to the citizens of the city for the collection, removal and disposal of refuse accumulated within the city, the city may enter into a contract with an independent provider, either private or another municipal corporate entity, for such services.
(Ord. No. 2023-014, § 1, 5-23-2023)
687:
The city council may negotiate with an independent service provider or another municipal corporate entity the terms, conditions and consideration to be paid for the services sought under such a contract; and it shall be presumed that any consideration agreed upon between the city and such independent service provider or municipal corporate entity shall be in the best interest and welfare of the city.
(Ord. No. 2023-014, § 1, 5-23-2023)
688:
(a) The city council shall have the exclusive right to award the collection, removal and disposal of residential solid waste within the city limits. No private individual, business, agent or other operation shall be permitted to haul solid waste produced by owners, occupants, tenants and lessees of residential buildings and premises for residential property and premises without first having obtained permission from the city council.
(b) Any person or company desiring such permission shall bid on the service during times specified, giving the details of operation and any charges to be made, all as may be required by the council and, where allowed, may negotiate such additional terms and conditions. Once a contract is issued by the council for such operations, the contract shall be issued in the name of the applicant. The council shall have full authority to make any other reasonable regulations relating to the hauling of solid waste over city streets and thoroughfares by independent collectors.
(Ord. No. 2023-014, § 1, 5-23-2023)
689:
The public works director, or designee, shall divide the city area into collection areas and routes, with areas and routes plainly outlined on a map of the city and listed numerically. The director shall prepare a list of the names of all the streets, roads, alleys, drives, highways and other public thoroughfares within each such route and shall provide such map and lists for the city clerk for public inspection. No neighborhood shall be split by collection day by a solid waste route.
(Ord. No. 2023-014, § 1, 5-23-2023)
690:
(a) The public works director, or designee, may from time to time prepare collection schedules designating days for collection of residential refuse, yard debris, and bulk goods wastes to present to the city manager for approval.
(b) Where strict application of this chapter would create an undue hardship, the public works director may, in his discretion, authorize a variance up to 90 days from the strict application of this chapter except where payments are required. The city manager may grant or deny a variance beyond the initial 90 days. No variance shall exceed one-year.
(Ord. No. 2023-014, § 1, 5-23-2023)
691:
(a) This chapter shall be enforced by city code enforcement officials, the city manager, or designee. Enforcement authority shall include the power to determine compliance with this chapter, to investigate complaints of violations of this chapter, and to pursue violations in any court of competent jurisdiction.
(b) The provisions of this chapter regarding the disposal or onsite burial of solid waste may be enforced by the Georgia Department of Natural Resources, Environmental Protection Division.
(c) Nothing in this chapter shall affect the ability of the city to pursue any remedies against any person and/or entity under local, state, or federal law.
(d) Nothing in this chapter shall affect the ability of the city to pursue the remedies available to it by virtue of its police powers.
(1) The director of public works, code enforcement officers, and/or police officers are authorized and directed to make inspections for the orderly compliance with this section and to issue citations for any violation of this section.
(2) All law enforcement agencies, officers and officials of this state or any political subdivision thereof, or any enforcement agency, officer or any official of any commission of this state or any political subdivision thereof, are hereby authorized, empowered and directed to enforce compliance with this chapter.
(3) Upon affidavit being made, the property owner, tenant, occupant, person in possession, or person creating the offensive and noisome act shall be served with a citation by the city police department and allowed to show cause, if any, why such person should not be found guilty of the offense, and upon conviction for failure to show good cause, shall be subject to punishment as provided in accordance with this chapter or as applicable under state law.
(Ord. No. 2023-014, § 1, 5-23-2023)
692:
If a property owner has not removed all nonconforming solid waste or yard debris from a public right of ways or easements within 48 hours after notification by the public works director, or designee, the public works director or designee may order such removal and all actual costs incurred plus a $50.00 administrative fee shall be billed to the property owner(s) or occupant(s).
(Ord. No. 2023-014, § 1, 5-23-2023)
693:
(a) Whenever litter is thrown, deposited, dropped, or dumped from any vehicle, boat, or other conveyance in violation of this chapter, it shall be prima facie evidence that the operator of the conveyance has violated this chapter.
(b) Except as provided in subsection (a) of this section, whenever any litter which is dumped, deposited, thrown or left on public or private property in violation of this article is discovered to contain any articles including, but not limited to documentation which display the name of the person thereon in such a manner as to indicate that the article belongs or belonged to such person, it shall be a presumption that such person has violated this chapter.
(Ord. No. 2023-014, § 1, 5-23-2023)
694:
Hearings for all violations of this chapter shall be held in the municipal court of the City of South Fulton, unless the prosecuting attorney, solicitor or municipal court judges determines that a conflict exists or improper venue and/or jurisdiction.
(Ord. No. 2023-014, § 1, 5-23-2023)
695:
(a) No individual, partnership, corporation or other entity shall engage in solid waste handling except in such a manner as to conform to and comply with this chapter and all applicable state and federal legislation, rules, regulations and orders.
(b) It shall be a violation of this chapter for any person, not approved by the city, to collect and haul any refuse or recyclables other than that arising from his own accumulation.
(Ord. No. 2023-014, § 1, 5-23-2023)
696:
Any person who violates any provision of this chapter may, upon conviction, incur a fine not to exceed $1,000.00 for each offense and/or community service not to exceed ten days. Each day a violation of this chapter continues shall be considered a separate and distinct offense.
Violators shall be cited and, upon conviction thereof, shall be punished as follows:
(1) By a fine of not less than $200.00 and not more than $1,000.00.
(2) In addition to the fine set out of this section, the violator shall reimburse the city for the reasonable cost of removing the litter when the litter is or is ordered removed by the city.
(3) At the sound discretion of the court, the person may be directed to pick up and remove:
a. From any public street or highway or public right-of-way for a distance not to exceed one mile any litter he has deposited and any and all litter deposited thereon by anyone else prior to the date of execution of sentence; or
b. Any and all litter from any public property, private right-of-way, or with prior permission of the legal owner or tenant in lawful possession of such property, any private property upon which it can be established by competent evidence that the person has deposited litter.
(Ord. No. 2023-014, § 1, 5-23-2023)
697:

709:
All terminology used in this article, not defined below, shall be in conformance with applicable publications of the American National Standards Institute (ANSI) or its successor body. The following words and terms, when used in this article, shall have the following meanings:
A-weighting is the electronic filtering in sound level meters that models human hearing frequency sensitivity.
Background sound level is the total sound pressure level in the area of interest excluding the noise source of interest.
Commercial or business property category is all property which is used primarily for the sale of merchandise or goods, or for the performances of service, or for office or clerical work. Any property zoned multi-use, as that term may be used in chapter 27 shall be deemed commercial or business property under this chapter.
Construction is any site preparation, assembly, erection, repair, alteration or similar action, or demolition of buildings or structures.
C-weighting is the electronic filtering in sound level meters that minimally attenuates very low frequencies.
Daytime hours shall mean the hours of 7:00 a.m. to 11:00 p.m., Monday through Thursday, 7:00 a.m. to 11:59 p.m. Friday, 9:00 a.m. to 11:59 p.m. Saturday, and 9:00 a.m. to 11:00 p.m. Sunday.
Decibel (dB) is the unit of measurement for sound pressure level at a specified location.
dBA is the A-weighted unit of sound pressure level.
dBC is the C-weighted unit of sound pressure level.
Emergency is any occurrence or set or set of circumstances involving actual or imminent physical trauma or property damage which demands immediate action.
Emergency work is any work or action performed for the purpose of preventing or alleviating the physical trauma or property damage threatened or caused by an emergency.
Fireworks is any combustible or explosive composition or any substance or combination of substances or article prepared for the purpose of producing a visible or audible effect by combustion, explosion, deflagration, or detonation, including blank cartridges, firecrackers, torpedoes, skyrockets, bombs, and other combustibles and explosives of like construction, as well as articles containing any explosive or flammable compound and tablets and other devices containing an explosive substance.
Impulsive sound is a sound having a duration of less than one second with an abrupt onset and rapid decay.
Industrial or manufacturing property category is any property which is used primarily for manufacturing or processing.
Institutional property category is any property which is used primarily for public purposes such as city hall or a city park.
Muffler is a sound-dissipative device or system for attenuating the sound of escaping gases of an internal combustion engine where such a device is part of the normal configuration of the equipment.
Multifamily dwelling is any building or other shelter that has been divided into separate units to house more than one family.
Nighttime shall mean the hours of 11:00 p.m. 7:00 a.m., Monday through Friday, 12:00 a.m. to 9:00 a.m. Saturday, and 12:00 a.m. to 9:00 a.m. Sunday.
Noise is any sound which annoys or disturbs humans or causes or tends to cause an adverse psychological or physiological effect on humans.
Noise disturbance is any sound that:
(1) Endangers the safety or health of any person;
(2) Disturbs a reasonable person of normal sensitivities; or
(3) Endangers personal or real property.
Noise-sensitive facility means any facility whose operations may be detrimentally impacted by excessive sound levels. Such facilities include, but are not limited to, schools, hospitals, and places of worship.
Octave band is all the components in a sound spectrum whose frequencies are between two sine waves components separated by an octave.
Real property line is the line, including its vertical extension that separates one parcel of real property from another.
Residential property category is all property established as a residential zoning category by the Zoning Ordinances of the City of South Fulton, except for multi-use zoning categories where there may be residential components.
Sound level meter (SLM) is an instrument used to measure sound pressure levels conforming to type 1 or type 2 standards as specified in ANSI Standard S1.4-1983 or the latest version thereof.
Sound pressure level (SPL) is 20 multiplied by the logarithm, to the base ten, of the measured sound pressure divided by the sound pressure associated with the threshold of human hearing, in units of decibels.
(Ord. No. 2018-010, 1, 2-27-2018)
